approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, scored survivors. It keeps the highest-scoring molecules in score and admission order, chooses breeding parents from high-ranked score bands, and builds fresh structures through connected-fragment crossover and local atom and bond mutations. The first parent supplies the ordinary mutation source or the usually larger crossover core; a separately drawn partner supplies the usually smaller graft. Ordinary multistep mutation and optional crossover finishing remain active, while direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Canonical identity checks form a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete task-local accepted-score archive uses counts of molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws choose pool members for evaluation. Accepted offspring update both the model and the live breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove unequal rank probabilities only from the first-parent draw, while preserving exactly the molecules that this draw can already select. The partner keeps its original score-band rule and exclusion of the chosen first molecule. The earlier control made both roles uniform on their original supports, and another also admitted previously unsupported survivors; neither identifies the first role separately. A balanced first-parent scheduler preserved rank preferences but changed dependence between draws, so it addresses a different question. This control keeps independent requests and changes only first-parent rank preference. The prediction is weaker average source quality and possibly lower final scores; the experiment will determine that role's conditional contribution, including any null or beneficial removal result.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting uncertainty is whether the Parent's concentration on high-ranked first parents is productive or merely repeats familiar mutation sources and crossover cores. The actual per-seed summary.json and run.log files for n-62daf219c70a all report completion: macro mean 0.5956696497334577, population SD 0.02659287062806747, and seed macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313. Its full published analysis reports 629 best-parent beats among 4,350 accepted offspring, 258 sequential incumbent improvements and 2,401 distinct offspring later used for breeding. Those counts do not isolate either parental role. The current positive contribution interpretation for n-f30747ffdbf8 establishes useful nonuniform weights on the original support when both roles are changed: 108,254 nonuniform requests, exact support preservation, 103,018 coupled identity differences, 4,020 exposed accepted offspring, and complete paired macro delta -0.05700288256234002. Nevertheless, parent beats rose to 936 while mean best-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.383214 and mean offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.321688. The broader uniform-live control n-a56491c332aa loses 0.04599801243765703 and changes both support and weights. The same-Parent first-parent scheduler n-f68f386d4d9d preserves prospective rank marginals, raises supported first-parent coverage from 24.32 to 29.00 and local wins to 720, but loses 0.04216145214436932. Earlier similarity-weighted partners n-a20706504e8f, core-balanced parents n-69c038cb49ac and success-weighted parents n-030a6ccbba7c also show allocation changes without endpoint improvement on their different binary-posterior Parent. Thus broader participation and easier local parent comparisons are inadequate measures of productive search. The unresolved behavior is the conditional value of the original first-parent rank concentration with partner weighting retained; the existing all-role evidence cannot localize it.
hypothesis: Remove nonuniform rank weighting only from each actual first-parent request by sampling uniformly over its exact original positive support after the inherited passive band draw, while retaining the original active score-quantile law and identity exclusion for every crossover-partner request.

finding_summary.headline: First-parent rank preference contributes: its removal lowers mean final Top-1 by 0.072496
finding_summary.insights:
The result localizes useful rank preference to the first-parent role while the crossover partner keeps its original law. Earlier removal from both roles could not establish that distinction. This is positive conditional contribution of first-parent rank weights in the tested composition and three-seed panel; it does not determine the partner’s contribution or permit subtraction of the shared-baseline controls into independent effects. The first parent supplies both ordinary mutation and crossover cores, so their separate values remain open.

More local wins did not mean better search. Strict best-parent beats rose from 629 to 819 and distinct accepted offspring later reused rose from 2,401 to 2,511, but mean best-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.372509 and mean offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.303045. Sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 237, with mean positive gain falling from 0.022510 to 0.019917. The easier parent reference explains why win counts alone would misread the outcome. Molecular inspection finds abundant rings, aromaticity and recognizable amine/carbonyl arrangements alongside reactive attachments and unresolved geometry and stereochemistry. Larger, decorated families did not consistently reproduce the Parent’s useful compact arrangements, but conventional-bond high-scoring counterexamples remain. Those associations narrow the search-quality problem without establishing a chemical cause of the loss. The fixed first-parent control now has an informative answer; support-only value, chemical mediation, the partner-only control and whole-foundation contribution remain open.
finding_summary.results:
Every one of 74,353 first-parent requests preserved the original eligible molecules while changing their probabilities; 71,068 actual identities differed from the inherited choice on the same random state. All 33,811 partner requests retained their original conditional law. Expected first-parent score on the actual populations fell from 0.359600 to 0.334474, and expected topness fell from 0.884224 to 0.755392. Changed first choices reached 3,926 of 4,350 accepted offspring; 2,211 of those offspring later bred. Full accepted-score learning, bounded greedy survival, ordinary graph transformations and all 435 complete candidate-pool selections remained active.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.523174, a paired change of -0.072496 against the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro changes were -0.156631, -0.029176 and -0.031680. Eleven of fifteen endpoints declined. Four improved: zaleplon seeds 0 and 2 (+0.075655 and +0.010925), median similarity seed 1 (+0.013577), and sitagliptin seed 1 (+0.124636). Four task means declined; zaleplon rose by 0.001980. Macro population SD increased from 0.026593 to 0.041376. All task runs completed with their full oracle budgets and no posterior fallback.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain reactive attachments and unspecified stereochemistry; larger structures do not ensure better scores
molecular.overall_character: Algorithm Node n-be83d2b1a4bd produces substituted indole amides and imines, linked nitrogen heterocycles, aryl/cyclic amines, medium-ring carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/dione heterocycles. Rings and aromaticity are abundant: the digest ring-closure incidences range from 0.9460 to 0.9782 and aromatic-text incidences from 0.9425 to 0.9736. These count proposal strings containing a feature, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Every task has 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. All recorded evaluated optimizer proposal strings parse with the available RDKit; graph parsing does not establish synthesis or stability. Halogen-text incidence ranges from 0.2448 to 0.9897, while explicit charge and stereocentre-text incidence are 0.0 throughout. Clearly protonatable amine candidates are present despite neutral notation. Many saturated and bridged centres have unspecified configuration. The overall chemistry is synthetically questionable and weak in drug-likeness because conventional aromatic, amide and amine regions coexist with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, peroxides, highly decorated structures and difficult ring junctions. This is not universal: the high-scoring aryl/azetidine family lacks N-halogen, O-halogen and peroxide bonds, and ordinary N-H indole amides also occur. Diversity is moderate across tasks and seeds but leading examples often belong to close local families; different strings are not evidence of independent scaffold coverage. All 15 Child trajectories and all 15 published Parent trajectories were read in full; no supplied path is missing and no task is omitted. Every digest excerpt was reconciled with its Child trajectory. Parent n-62daf219c70a paths match the published-path template in context.evidence_index. The immutable request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. Comparisons below use those published Parent records, not the changing worktree as Parent authority. Conditions are Research in Depth epoch 1, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task/seed. The Parent baseline reproduced historical n-c55c3d520a2c chemistry under its new profile; the original gap reports in both indexed nodes were read, and their source is retained in the transferable gaps. Historical identity is not an additional independent current comparison. Digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals rather than all seeds' retained best molecules; full trajectories supply the other seeds and best-score pairs. Scores below are observed values rounded to six decimal places unless scientific notation is needed. Heavy-atom and ring counts are RDKit readings of the cited records. Chemistry associations describe output only; they do not establish a missing target pharmacophore, component attribution, activation, biological activity or contribution. The audit and complete path/hash inventory are in .slots/round-0023-slot-2/molecular/trajectory_audit.json.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader is a 25-heavy-atom, three-aromatic-ring indole carboxanilide carrying methylamino, methoxymethyl, aryl fluorine and N-chloro-amide groups. Seed 1 instead favors a similarly sized N-amino indole/aryl ketimine with methoxy and fluoromethyl substituents. Seed 2 reaches a 25-heavy-atom partially unsaturated six-membered N-chloro heterocycle linked to an anilide and an O-linked cyanate side chain; its leading structure has two rings, only one aromatic. Thus not every leader is a fully aromatic indole. Mean proposal SMILES length is 43.1, ring-closure incidence 0.9609 and aromatic-text incidence 0.9425. Familiar aryl/amide frameworks coexist with N-halogen, N-N, cyanate and unsaturated ether chemistry; the conventional annulated N-H indole anilide at seed 0 evaluation 169 is a counterexample to any claim that all useful output needs those attachments. Published Parent leaders are also compact aromatic frameworks, but include an N-hydroxy pyridyl amide, an indole-linked diketone, and a cumulene/imine family rather than these exact Child seed families.
liabilities: The highest seed-0 molecule has chlorine on the amide nitrogen, chemically distinct from its ordinary carbon-bound aryl fluorine.
The seed-2 family contains N-Cl and O-linked cyanate groups, while other leaders have N-N substitution or imines. Their scores are not stability or synthetic-route evidence.
Tiny late proposals lose almost all functional context; extensive unsaturated substituent changes can also reduce the score while leaving a recognizable scaffold.
missing_features: Conventional local alternatives preserving the best compact aromatic/polar arrangement are not consistently represented at the leading scores; ordinary N-H amides already exist, so this is not inability to make an amide or indole.

Chemically independent plausible frameworks with the same favorable arrangement are scarce among leaders within each seed; the observed structures do not identify an exact missing target-specific motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Complete observed Child / published Parent best-score pairs are seed 0: 0.469707 at evaluation 262 / 0.394051 at evaluation 289; seed 1: 0.393477 at evaluation 114 / 0.474117 at evaluation 293; seed 2: 0.449897 at evaluation 250 / 0.438973 at evaluation 294. The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.305105. The Child seed-0 fluorinated N-chloro-amide leader scores 0.469707, versus 0.440491 for its otherwise matching unfluorinated pendant phenyl analogue at evaluation 282. This is a local substitution association. In seed 2, Br-, Cl- and F-anilides at evaluations 250, 284 and 286 all score 0.449897; halogen identity is not uniformly rewarded. Removing that anilide aryl group and retaining an N-fluoro amide at evaluation 296 gives 0.005635; the halogenated heterocyclic core alone is insufficient. Ethene at seed 1 evaluation 269 scores 0.0. The N-H annulated anilide at seed 0 evaluation 169 scores 0.396974 without a heteroatom-halogen bond. Seed-2 evaluation 300 scores 0.251258 despite retaining a pyrrole/aryl-amide framework and unsaturated ether substituents. The visible reward concerns a compact combination and placement of aromatic and polar regions, not simply more aromaticity or a mandatory reactive bond.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader has 29 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, three aromatic: a cyclopropane-annulated indole-like region joined through a thioamide to a diazine ring, with both ring-N-F and side-chain-N-F attachments, aryl chlorine and carbon-bound fluorine. Seeds 1 and 2 favor much larger linked aromatic/heterocyclic assemblies: their leaders have 47 and 53 heavy atoms. Seed 1 combines an oxygen/nitrogen carbonyl heterocycle, multiple aryl regions, imidic side-chain chemistry and an N-fluoro heteroaromatic group. Seed 2 carries a fused dione, another nitrogen heterocycle, polyenyl substituents, chloromethyl ethers, O-F and an acyl fluoride. Mean proposal SMILES length is 91.3, maximum 238, ring-closure incidence 0.9713 and aromatic-text incidence 0.9713. These are not ring-poor candidates; elaboration and local reactivity are the concerns. The published Parent seed-0 leader is a 30-heavy-atom linked fused aza-aromatic carbonyl/thione structure, while Parent seeds 1 and 2 have other aza-aromatic and decorated aryl families. The Parent also contains questionable reactive groups and is not a chemical-quality standard.
liabilities: The annulated three-membered carbocycle shares an edge with the aromatic framework and merits a geometry assessment; ring closure and aromatic notation alone do not establish feasibility.
N-F, O-F, peroxide, chloromethyl-ether and acyl-fluoride environments appear in high or late examples. Carbon-bound fluorine should not be conflated with those attachments.
Large flexible decorated structures and tiny floor-scoring fragments coexist, so both excess elaboration and loss of connected context remain visible.
missing_features: The current output does not show a comparably rewarded compact alternative to the Parent seed-0 linked nitrogen-ring architecture; this does not establish that copying one Parent scaffold or adding more ring nitrogens is the answer.

Consistent simplification while retaining useful connected heterocyclic context is missing from the large leading families, although the smaller seed-1 relative demonstrates that this chemistry is possible.
Stable peripheral alternatives and credible strained-ring geometry are not established for the leading thioamide family; synthetic accessibility was not measured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Complete observed Child / published Parent best-score pairs are seed 0: 0.603470 at evaluation 286 / 0.856148 at evaluation 281; seed 1: 0.597187 at evaluation 267 / 0.624821 at evaluation 296; seed 2: 0.597173 at evaluation 296 / 0.617802 at evaluation 296. The initial aryl/fused-dione molecule scores 0.548381, while tiny chlorine and ethynylated N-O fragments reach the observed 0.5 floor. The Child seed-0 methoxy leader scores 0.603470; inserting an O-O linkage in its methoxy substituent at evaluation 299 still gives 0.601476. This score tolerates that local liability. More size is not sufficient: the 47-heavy-atom seed-1 leader scores 0.597187, whereas its smaller, structurally related amide/heterocycle at evaluation 294 scores 0.593733 without N-halogen or O-halogen attachments. That is a useful simplification counterexample, not an isolated size experiment. The 53-heavy-atom seed-2 leader scores 0.597173 and the more extended final proposal scores 0.596391. Parent seed 0 reaches 0.856148 in a compact but chemically different nitrogen-ring organization. The output therefore supports sensitivity to heterocycle/linkage organization rather than reward for size or halogenation alone; it cannot locate the responsible structural feature.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2 produces the most conventionally recognizable high-scoring family: two substituted phenyl rings connected through a phenethyl tertiary azetidine and a partially unsaturated nitrogen six-membered ring. Its leader has 30 heavy atoms and four rings, two aromatic, with phenol, methoxy and carbon-bound aryl fluorine; it has no N-halogen, O-halogen or peroxide bond. Seed 1 instead favors a 32-heavy-atom flexible diaminoalkyl/two-aryl structure with a substituted cyclopentadiene. Seed 0 retains a 38-heavy-atom polyamine/aryl-thioether structure with an N-chloro diazacycle, a dihalogenated saturated carbon and a sulfur-oxygen side chain. The full output is broader in size than these leaders: mean SMILES length 71.6, maximum 230; ring-closure incidence 0.9782, aromatic-text incidence 0.9736 and halogen incidence 0.9897. The best seed-2 family has a medicinally recognizable amine/aryl organization, but its azetidine substitution and unsaturated ring still need synthetic and configurational assessment. Parent seed leaders include both acyclic tertiary aryl amines and saturated cyclic amines with aryl ether or fused thioether regions; the Child is not globally unable to generate basic amine centres.
liabilities: The better family still contains a substituted azetidine and a nonaromatic unsaturated nitrogen ring with unassigned stereochemical identity; an ordinary small ring is not automatically infeasible.
Seed-0 leaders and late products contain N-Cl or unusual sulfur/heteroatom environments, and seed-1 late products can contain O-Cl; these liabilities are not shared by the seed-2 leader.
The high incidence of carbon-bound halogens and substantial aromatic content call for property assessment, but lipophilicity, solubility and toxicity were not measured here.
missing_features: The favorable compact aryl/amine/linker arrangement is not consistently recovered across seeds; seed 0 keeps larger reactive decoration despite already containing amines. The gap is not absence of ring amines.

Configuration at substituted saturated centres and appropriate protonation identity are unspecified in the emitted strings. Neutral notation is not evidence that protonatable centres are absent or that the oracle used a particular protonation state.
Equally useful plausible alternatives to the dominant within-seed aryl/amine family remain limited; these records do not identify one obligatory ring size or target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Complete observed Child / published Parent best-score pairs are seed 0: 0.547856 at evaluation 275 / 0.999999 at evaluation 284; seed 1: 0.821158 at evaluation 271 / 0.996975 at evaluation 261; seed 2: 0.989715 at evaluation 255 / 0.999993 at evaluation 241. The Child seed-2 phenethyl azetidine at evaluation 255 scores 0.989715, versus 0.938038 for the corresponding benzyl-linked analogue at evaluation 239; the extra linker methylene is favorable in this particular scaffold. The low seed-2 evaluation 13 N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine carboxamide scores 0.000256, and dimethyl ether at evaluation 243 scores 0.004246. Having nitrogen or an aromatic ring alone is therefore insufficient; accessible amine candidates in the appropriate aryl/linker arrangement are associated with much higher scores. Seed 0 ends with a heavily heteroatom-decorated polycycle scoring 0.085331 despite retaining amines and aromatic rings, whereas its own best is 0.547856. The high-scoring Child and Parent families without heteroatom-halogen attachments directly counter any universal requirement for those bonds. Neither the near-ceiling scores nor this structural association demonstrates experimentally confirmed binding or a component-specific chemical pathway.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 molecule has 32 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, two aromatic. It combines a propyl/ethoxy-substituted aniline region with a fused nitrogen-containing system carrying an N-methyl lactam and a ketone; the nonaromatic rings include seven-membered rings. Seed 0 reaches a 32-heavy-atom bridged aza-aromatic/dicarbonyl architecture; seed 2 reaches a 34-heavy-atom linked aza-aromatic and bridged carbonyl system with an N-O linkage and seven-/eight-membered rings. Mean proposal SMILES length is 54.8, ring-closure incidence 0.9759 and aromatic-text incidence 0.9667. Halogen incidence is 0.2448, far below the other tasks, and all seed leaders lack N-halogen/O-halogen/peroxide bonds. Functional groups look more familiar than in the highly halogenated families, but complex junctions and unassigned saturated centres still make synthesis uncertain. Published Parent leaders also combine alkoxy aza-aromatics with cyclic carbonyl/amine regions and medium-ring bridges; both sides have rich ring chemistry rather than an absent scaffold vocabulary.
liabilities: Multiple fused/bridged medium rings create difficult connectivity and stereochemical questions even when individual amide and amine groups are conventional.
The seed-2 leader contains an N-O-acyl-connected region, which warrants a local stability assessment rather than being treated as an ordinary tertiary amide.
Many useful examples lack reactive halogen bonds, so a universal halogen-based explanation would miss this family; late low-context fragments and elaborated variants remain separate problems.
missing_features: Chemically simpler alternatives retaining the favorable aromatic/alkoxy and cyclic polar-group relationships are not well demonstrated among the best within-seed structures; increasing ring count alone is not the missing feature.

The bridged and medium-ring molecules lack explicit stereochemical identity and demonstrated feasible conformations. The observed modest scores do not identify an exact missing target structure or donor/acceptor count.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Complete observed Child / published Parent best-score pairs are seed 0: 0.208445 at evaluation 300 / 0.225840 at evaluation 293; seed 1: 0.234987 at evaluation 281 / 0.221410 at evaluation 278; seed 2: 0.219663 at evaluation 297 / 0.226003 at evaluation 261. The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.167839, while the seed-1 lactam/ketone leader scores 0.234987. Its bridged relative at evaluation 233 scores 0.227402 and a rearranged cyclic relative at evaluation 293 scores 0.222376. The final seed-1 proposal has more perceived rings than the leader but scores 0.207174; these are different connectivities, not a controlled ring-count contrast. Seed 2 similarly ends at 0.185249 after reaching 0.219663. Difluorine at seed 0 evaluation 260 scores 0.0. The observed gradient favors a particular combination of aromatic/alkoxy and cyclic carbonyl/nitrogen environments over disconnected-in-function tiny fragments, while indiscriminate bridging or nitrogen enrichment is not uniformly rewarded. The Child seed-1 best exceeds its matched Parent while seeds 0 and 2 do not; a single chemistry narrative cannot erase those counterexamples.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 28 heavy atoms and three perceived aromatic rings: a fused nitrogen dione linked to a fluorophenyl group, an aldehyde/fluoroalkyl side chain, ring-N-F and an aminomethyl-N-F substituent. Another leading seed-1 variant substitutes a fluorinated cyclobutene/aldehyde and halodiene. Seed 0 favors a 24-heavy-atom aryl fused imino/carbonyl heterocycle with N-F and N-OH attachments. Seed 2 instead reaches a 25-heavy-atom four-ring imino/carbonyl framework with a fused cyclobutene, an imine side chain, fluoroethyl and N-F. A distinct 26-heavy-atom seed-2 nitrile/fluoroalkyl analogue is a strong counterexample to an obligatory N-F bond. Mean proposal SMILES length is 46.8, ring-closure incidence 0.9460, aromatic-text incidence 0.9448 and halogen incidence 0.8667. These are compact polar fluorinated heterocycles, not simply underdeveloped hydrocarbons, but their reactive substitution and small unsaturated-ring junctions compromise apparent plausibility. Published Parent leaders use related imino/dione chemistry; the Parent seed-2 best instead has a small cyclic cumulene attached to a larger aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring, a different and concerning geometry.
liabilities: N-F bonds on ring nitrogen and aminomethyl nitrogen, aldehydes and imines appear in leading examples; the ordinary carbon-bound fluorines of the N-F-free counterexample are chemically different.

Cyclobutene and fused small-ring junctions need geometry assessment, and configuration is unspecified. The severe cyclic-cumulene example belongs to the Parent comparison and should not be misreported as this Child leader.
A good score for one compact analogue does not establish a general size window; the observed near-zero bulky and tiny examples differ in many chemical features.
missing_features: Conventional substituent and ring-topology alternatives that preserve the favorable compact polar/fluoroalkyl organization are not consistently shown at the best scores. The high-scoring N-F-free nitrile family proves that part of this capability already exists.
Explicit stereochemical, tautomeric and conformational identity is missing for potentially stereogenic fluorinated and bridged centres; aromatic labels alone do not supply that identity.

These trajectories do not reveal a unique missing pharmacophore or justify importing a named ligand scaffold. Better chemical feasibility and better recorded reward remain separate, untested requirements.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Complete observed Child / published Parent best-score pairs are seed 0: 0.514425 at evaluation 178 / 0.651021 at evaluation 276; seed 1: 0.611642 at evaluation 284 / 0.487006 at evaluation 290; seed 2: 0.588806 at evaluation 300 / 0.720885 at evaluation 273. The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.002094. A bulky 48-heavy-atom linked oxygenated/dione proposal at seed 0 evaluation 15 scores 6.593933252035046e-30, while isolated fluorine at seed 1 evaluation 282 scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. Both excessive elaboration and near-total context loss can therefore fail. The leading compact N-fluorinated dione scores 0.611642. The seed-2 nitrile analogue without N-F scores 0.584214; its otherwise matching N-fluoromethyl relative at evaluation 261 scores 0.568822, so extending that particular substituent to fluoroethyl helps locally. It does not show a universal fluorination or size rule. The Child seed-1 family exceeds its Parent counterpart, whereas seeds 0 and 2 do not. Parent seed 2 reaches 0.720885 in the cyclic-cumulene structure; that association neither proves such geometry feasible nor implies that it is required. The visible gradient concerns balanced compact fluorinated/polar organization and substituent context, not merely nitrogen count or mandatory N-F chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced in baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed here in n-be83d2b1a4bd under Research in Depth epoch 1, Search Seeds 0/1/2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task/seed. Current leaders include an N-chloro indole amide, N-fluorinated thioamide-linked heterocycles and N-fluorinated diones. A methoxy-to-peroxide relative still scores 0.601476 beside its 0.603470 methoxy structural counterpart. In contrast, the 0.989715 aryl/azetidine molecule lacks N-halogen, O-halogen and peroxide bonds, and ordinary N-H amides also occur. The recurring gap is local bond environment, not absence of useful heterocycles or a universal problem with carbon-bound halogens.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments while retaining useful aromatic and polar-group relationships.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs chemically contextual alternatives that can retain favorable scaffold relationships without automatically inheriting reactive attachments. Preserve ordinary aryl halogens and useful amine centres when supported by local feedback. This suggests testing environmental plausibility, not a blanket halogen filter; these associations neither establish a score benefit for replacement nor attribute the chemistry to one component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced in baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed here in n-be83d2b1a4bd under Research in Depth epoch 1, Search Seeds 0/1/2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task/seed. The historical source includes a severe cyclic-cumulene example; that exact geometry is not the current leader. Current leaders instead include a cyclopropane-annulated aromatic edge, a fused cyclobutene and several medium-ring bridged carbonyl frameworks. Conventional cyclic amines also attain high scores, and extra ring connections can accompany lower scores. Thus rich ring content survives while geometric feasibility remains unestablished.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently distinguish a valid ring graph from a geometrically credible unsaturation pattern and ring junction.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need awareness of bond geometry, ring size and bridge connectivity, alongside plausible alternative topologies preserving learned functional relationships. Ordinary azetidines, fused systems and small rings should be distinguished from unsupported strained arrangements. Parsing and aromatic labels cannot substitute for this information, and no endpoint advantage or component-specific source of the issue is established.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced in baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed here in n-be83d2b1a4bd under Research in Depth epoch 1, Search Seeds 0/1/2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task/seed. The digest stereocentre-string rate is 0.0 in every current task. Substituted azetidines, fluorinated ring centres and bridged carbonyl frameworks nevertheless contain potential stereogenic environments. Neutral-charge notation is also universal, while ordinary protonatable amine candidates are clearly present; charge absence is a separate issue.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereochemical identity unspecified after creating potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and graph transformations need to preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemistry where chemically meaningful, accounting for achiral and configurationally unstable cases. Protonation and tautomerism require separate assessment rather than an assumption from neutral SMILES. The evidence establishes unspecified identity, not a measured stereochemical penalty or a demonstrated gain from enumeration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced in baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed here in n-be83d2b1a4bd under Research in Depth epoch 1, Search Seeds 0/1/2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task/seed. Tiny late hydrocarbon and halogen proposals reach recorded floors, while some linked heterocyclic families expand to heavily decorated large structures. Current 47- and 53-heavy-atom leaders are not intrinsically better than compact alternatives; a smaller related amide/heterocycle scores 0.593733 beside a 0.597187 larger leader. A separate 48-heavy-atom proposal scores 6.593933252035046e-30, while a compact 28-heavy-atom dione reaches 0.611642. These are context-dependent comparisons, not isolated effects of atom count.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain useful connected molecular context while avoiding excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local feedback can guide transformations that preserve relevant connected functional groups while allowing simplification or replacement of dispensable regions. The missing capability is consistent chemical context control; neither a fixed minimum size nor a preference for larger molecules follows. More plausible or compact proposals still require observed score evidence, and this report assigns no causal responsibility to a component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced in baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed here in n-be83d2b1a4bd under Research in Depth epoch 1, Search Seeds 0/1/2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task/seed. Current high-scoring examples repeatedly modify indole amides, linked nitrogen heterocycles, aryl/cyclic amines or bridged carbonyl systems by changing peripheral halogens, short linkers and local ring connections. Distinct seeds do produce substantially different families, including both flexible and cyclic amines, and some Child families exceed their matched Parent examples. This supports limited within-family alternatives, not global structural collapse, inability to make rings or a universal failure of the current chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Leading output within a seed offers few chemically independent plausible alternatives to its recurring scaffold family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need feasible scaffold reorganizations that preserve favorable functional relationships learned from accepted observations. Distinct SMILES, extra ring closures or broad coverage alone are insufficient evidence of useful alternatives. Assess resulting chemistry and its own observed reward; these associations neither show that more diversity improves endpoints nor identify the responsible search component.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
